The full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 0 failures/errors).

## Summary

I implemented the GOLD tier rule with three small, localized edits — no controller methods touched and no schema files changed, keeping structural impact low:

1. **`HouseholdDuplicates.assignHousehold`** — now stamps *every* `sharesHousehold` owner with the deterministic household id (previously only owners joining an already-existing member), so all members of a household share one id. It also computes the household size at create time (`1 + existing members sharing the key`) and stores it on the new owner. This edit stays inside the small `HouseholdDuplicates` class (low surrounding complexity).

2. **`Owner`** — added a read-only `householdSize` field with a Hibernate `@Formula` (a correlated `count(*)` over matching `household_id`) plus a getter/setter. The `@Formula` populates the count on genuine DB loads; the setter lets the create path fill the in-session instance.

3. **`OwnerMapper`** — extended only the `membershipTier` mapping expression to return `"GOLD"` when `householdSize >= 3`, otherwise falling through to the existing SILVER/BRONZE logic unchanged.
